text:
Collin Graf is a 24-year-old who went undrafted, earned his way into San Jose's lineup out of Quinnipiac and is now getting a look beside the Sharks' best player: a reporter's post from Nov. 18 had him on a line with Macklin Celebrini and Stenberg.

The production hasn't matched the role yet. He has 3 goals and 2 assists in 24 games, a pace of 0.8 points per 60 minutes against a league average near 2.1 for forwards. But this is a case where the process is better than the results. He has 4.75 expected goals on his own shots, the quality-of-chance measure, and has scored 1.75 fewer goals than that. San Jose has also scored 2.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice.

Our talent range puts his true scoring rate somewhere between 1.5 and 2.1 points per 60, well above what he has shown. He gets to dangerous spots, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 52% of his shots last season coming off the rush. If the Celebrini look sticks, those chances should start to turn into points.
headline: Good chances, small returns
